scope.current_boundary: Define gravitational potential at a point as the work done per unit mass in bringing a small test mass from infinity to the point.
scope.previous_boundary_used: Use point-mass gravitational field strength and explain its approximate constancy close to Earth.
scope.next_boundary_checked: Use the point-mass gravitational-potential equation and connect potential to gravitational potential energy. Those equations are deliberately deferred.

questions_visited.why_selected: Requires the definition to explain the negative sign.

questions_visited.why_selected: Directly asks why potential near a point mass is negative.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Explain the sign using the reference at infinity and attractive gravity.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Moving towards the mass lowers potential below the zero reference.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Treating a negative potential as a negative mass or negative force magnitude.

questions_visited.why_selected: Tests explanation by explicit reference to the definition.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Show why the sign follows from work and the stated reference.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Infinity is zero; inward motion under attraction releases energy, so potential is negative.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Repeating the definition without explaining the sign.

questions_visited.why_selected: Applies the negative-potential explanation to a satellite position.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Transfer the sign reasoning to an orbiting object without confusing potential and potential energy.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Potential at every finite distance from an isolated attractive mass is below zero at infinity.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Assuming motion in orbit makes potential positive.
